# Model definition

### Sermon

A sermon is a text found in a manuscript. A excerpted (shortened) sermon is summarised as the full sermon, because not every sermon is correctly annotated as excerpted.

### Manuscript

- A manuscript is a set of authentic Augustinian sermons [se1, se2, se3 etc.], where all the inserted other sermons are invisible.

- A manuscript is the product of deliberate selection of existing sermons, because we see these sermons in earlier manuscripts and it takes time to write it down.

- A manuscript in this analysis is a observation of an co-occurrence of a set of sermons.

- A manuscript is created in one century and the mss with more or unknown centuries (n=11) are omitted.

### Edge

- An edge is created when two sermons co-occur in the same manuscript.

- The nodes are fully connected over all sermons in the same manuscript. N = (n - 1)\*n / 2

- The network is weighted by the sum of mss were the ego and alter co-occur

### Transformation to binary network

- Every century a new network is created to analysis the network dynamics

- A null model is created to analyse which sermons have connections that can also be expected from random change. In other words, two sermons are connected when they occur together in a manuscript more often than expected under a null model.

  - The null model preserves the manuscript size structure by swopping sermons between manuscripts before it is made into a network.

### Robustness check

- The uncertainty number per sermon is calculated per century.

  - Per century, check manuscripts with double literature and count the number of disputed sermons (certain - uncertain).

  - Randomly remove sermons in that rate in manuscripts without double literature.

  - Randomly remove [0, 0.2, 0.5, and 0.9] manuscripts.

  - Perform above mentioned null-model for final binary wave dataset.

## Statistics based on research question

- RQ1: Are two sermons that are connected on t0 more likely to be also connected on t1?

  - Stat: lagged tie persistance. It works on dyad level: tie survival, tie formation. Or Jaccard simiarity for outgoing ties effect (p. 138, statistic 16) or maintenance (endowment for creation) (31. p. 192)

- RQ2: Does sermons homophily on sermon level similarity contribute to forming or presistence of edges? (for features see: data_wrangling)

  - Stat: covariate effect (egoPlusAltX) (3. p. 167) or sameX (106. p. 155)

  - covariate-related similarity (simX, 96. p. 154) for LDA because similarity in latent space.

- RQ3: Do proposed collection and subcollection membership predict non-random co-occurance?

  - Stat: also same covariate =\> sameX (106. p. 155)

Potential:

- density effect (out-degree sum) -\> distribution of popularity of sermons

- cycle3 (hoeveel 3 circles zijn er) or number of dense triads -\> proxy for clusterings co-officient

- degree activity plus popularity effect (31. p. 166)

- Number of ministeps
